trust_decision.summary: Requests served over the HTTP API must not make the server fetch attacker-supplied image/audio/video URLs to private or loopback addresses, and must not let a server-originated media string read an arbitrary local file; the decision is made in mistralrs-server-core's media loaders (parse_image_url/parse_audio_url/parse_video_url and input_file.file_url), split by a policy so library/CLI callers keep local-file support.

landing_point.why: The summary names `image_url` in the media loader, so a reader greps image_url and lands on the chat-completions parser, which turns each parsed `image_url` string into a fetch through parse_image_url at line 931.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /v1/chat/completions (also /v1/messages, /v1/messages/count_tokens, /v1/responses and POST /mcp, all through parse_request)
same parse_request entry points, audio_url content part
same parse_request entry points, video_url content part
POST /v1/responses input_file.file_data (data: URL or raw base64)
public API mistralrs_server_core::util::parse_image_url (used by mistralrs-cli chat mode and embedded users)
all of the above, via the new shared loader load_media_source/fetch_remote_limited
crate wiring for the new media_source module (inserted after mistralrs-server-core/src/lib.rs:249)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Python bindings are a local in-process SDK: fetching arbitrary URLs and reading local files is the caller's own capability and the documented purpose, and the advisory is about the unauthenticated HTTP server.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: `parse_image_url`/`parse_audio_url`/`parse_video_url` are documented public APIs that accept local paths and file:// URLs; the CLI chat mode calls them with user paths. Rejecting file:// or private hosts inside the shared functions instead of behind a policy breaks local media loading outside the server.

O6_input_shapes: data: URL with base64 payload (image, audio, video)
bare local filesystem path (relative or absolute)
redirect chain: an allowed URL answering 302 with a Location to 127.0.0.1
input_file.file_data as raw base64 without a data: prefix
chat-completions shape {image_url:{url}} versus Responses shape image_url as a plain string
multiple media items per message (arrays of image_urls/audio_urls/video_urls)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: web-search tool fetches a URL directly when the model's query is a raw http(s) URL, with no private/loopback validation and default redirect following (a sibling sink of the same mechanism, not the media loader)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Web search is meant to fetch internet pages; the URL comes from the model's tool call rather than the request body, and the advisory names the media loader.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another crate (mistralrs-core) reached from the same POST /v1/chat/completions entry point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second URL-import path (e.g. an import_url on the /v1/files upload or container-file routes) reusing fetch_file_url
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Responses API already has file_url next to image_url; adding URL import to the file routes is a natural feature and would silently inherit the redirect/private-host gap.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new MCP tool that takes a media URL and fetches it outside parse_request
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The MCP server already wraps chat parsing on its own port; a dedicated media/resource tool is an obvious next step and would bypass the policy split.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third hand-copied parse_*_url for a new media type (e.g. PDF/document) in the Python bindings
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The crate already contains three copies of the same fetch logic, so another copy for a new modality matches existing style.

O9_family: SSRF and arbitrary local file read (CWE-918, CWE-73)
